Meera Patel: heads up — ran into an odd case where the edge fastpath drops to slowpath mid-stream and the client ends up retrying aggressively. wondering if we should annotate origin of retries in headers so downstream can make better choices :thinking_face:
Omar Khan: can you paste a short trace? is this because of an upstream 503 or because we moved to a different shard?
Meera Patel: trace snippet below, simplified:
```
EDGE: fastpath->slowpath handoff at t=12.34s
UPSTREAM: 200 then wire error "connection reset"
CLIENT: immediate retry without idempotency key
```
Laura Chen: if client retries without idempotency we can easily double-run side effects. We need a clear policy: either gateway suppresses client-originated retries mid-stream or it marks them.
Ben Hsu: what about tagging with `X-Retry-Origin: gateway|client|upstream`? gateway could set origin when it initiates a retry/fallback. lightweight and readable.
Omar Khan: I like the header but need to be careful: streaming bodies + large KV cache mean we can't buffer whole body to retry. For gateway-origin retries we rely on resumable stream tokens; for client-origin we should reject mid-stream retries unless idempotency token present.
Meera Patel: Agreed. Proposed rules: 1) If retry arrives before request commit (headers only), accept and coalesce. 2) If mid-stream and no idempotency header -> respond 409 with `Retry-Required: idempotency` and `X-Retry-Allowed: false`. 3) Gateway-origin retries get `X-Retry-Origin: gateway` and `X-Retry-Id: <uuid>`.
Laura Chen: minor nit — 409 feels heavy. Maybe 422 plus explanation? But ergonomics for SDKs matter. 409 is fine if we document it.
Ben Hsu: also add a TTL on `X-Retry-Id` so we don't hold cache entries forever. suggest `X-Retry-Id-TTL: 30s` on responses that permit mid-stream resume.
Meera Patel: +1 on TTL. Also we should surface metric: `edge.retry_origin.{gateway,client,upstream}` and `edge.retry_rejected_midstream` so we can see how often clients hit this.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: refactor/edge-retries annotated (PR #4123) — CI passed :white_check_mark:
Omar Khan: Implementation notes: we won't change client SDKs now. Gateway will set header only when it creates retries. For client retries we return the 409/422 guidance and include a short example in response body pointing to docs. That keeps behavior predictable today and gives time to evolve SDKs.
Meera Patel: ok I'll draft the RFC follow-up with examples and a small test harness that simulates a mid-stream fastpath->slowpath handoff. Will include sample curl responses and recommended SDK behavior. Thanks all :pray:
